tagline: Nine miles of interstate over the mountains to Sams Gap.
intro: It is nine miles of interstate, and the state counts it as a scenic byway. From Exit 9 at Mars Hill, I-26 climbs west through Madison County to Buckner Gap, then comes down to Sams Gap on the Tennessee line, where the Appalachian Trail passes under the highway and a small parking lot was built for its hikers.

The Madison County section opened in late 2003. Beneath it run two eight-foot concrete culverts that let bears, deer and other wildlife cross without setting foot on the road, and three runaway truck ramps line the eastbound side.

moments.title: First scenic overlook
moments.text: Just west of Exit 9, careful observers can pick out the Blue Ridge Parkway across the valley and the tiny California Creek Church below the highway.

moments.title: Buckner Gap
moments.text: At nearly 5,000 feet this is the highest point on any interstate in North Carolina, with one of the state's first monarch butterfly sanctuaries near the top, hard to see from the road.

moments.title: Laurel River bridge
moments.text: The bridge over the Laurel River near Wolf Laurel sits high enough, in hard enough winters, to need an automatic de-icing system, and its spray nozzles show along the sides.
